title: Release 0.7.0
body:
We've accumulated quite a few new features, so it's time for a release.

The only downside right now is that wheels from PyPI are not installable because `lonboard` upper-bounds `anywidgets`. I've opened developmentseed/lonboard#1271, but in the meantime there's nothing I can do about that besides pointing people to `conda-forge`, where the upper-bound does not exist. So instead I'll add a note to the changelog saying that people should install `lonboard=0.17.0b1` instead.

For reference, `anywidgets=0.11.0` introduced a much more stable way to compose with other widgets, which is such a big improvement that I'm not sure we can provide backwards compatibility. The easiest way forward would probably be to make the plotting libraries optional dependencies, but I don't have the time for that right now.

title: allow dggs implementations to customize the layers
body:
So far we've enforced using the same `SolidPolygonLayer` for all DGGS, but as pointed out in #187 this comes with some problems and is not the most performant because we need to generate polygons on the host and transfer to the browser.

Instead we can use specialized lonboard layers like the `H3HexagonLayer` for H3, which is guaranteed to be correct (or at least we can get someone else to take care of correctness) while keeping the `SolidPolygonLayer` as the default.

cc @relativityhd, I'm sorry it took me as long as it did to get back to this. This doesn't contain the other changes from #197, though.

Edit: also, this requires the indirect dependency on `h3-py` to be at least 4.5.0, otherwise `lonboard` triggers a bug in the h3 C library (degenerate polygons if the cells are in a specific order).

title: lazy cell id coordinates for the moc index
body:
The moc index strongly compresses the cell ids, so it doesn't really make sense that we need to have the cell ids in memory.

This adds a specialized `IndexingAdapter` that holds a reference to the `healpix_geo.nested.RangeMOCIndex` instance and is inspired by the `CoordinateTransform` mechanism in `xarray`. It has slightly different behavior, though:
- coordinates are only computed when explicitly converted (`values`, `data`, `compute()`, `load()`), slicing the coordinate will not compute
- the coordinate is strictly 1D, thus _vindex_get is not supported (for now, at least)
- transpose is either a no-op or raises because multiple values were passed

It also splits the `xdggs.healpix` module into a subpackage because it became too big to be convenient. I might also do the same for the tests (`xdggs/tests/test_healpix.py`).

body:
Bumps [pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish](https://github.com/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish) from 1.14.0 to 1.14.2.
Release notes

Sourced from pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish's releases.

v1.14.2

🛠️ Urgh… Another release!? Again? Explain yourself!

Looking at the diff, you'll only witness updates across the dependency tree. That's it! It's not a security fix or anything like that even, no. But you'll want this update.

[!tip] So what most people will find useful is @​takluyver💰's update of Twine to v7 that we use internally (#416). This version will let them upload their sdists and wheels containing core packaging metadata v2.5 to (Test)PyPI.

🧐 Tell me why..

TL;DR non-pure-python projects with C-extensions tend to have dozens (sometimes hundreds) wheels to upload to PyPI per release. They are often quite big and take time to transfer over the network. People started noticing problems and coming up with DIY sharding workarounds like aio-libs/aiohttp#13226 around July 23. On this date, projects with a good amount of bytes to publish would start getting timeouts 5 minutes after the PyPI publishing job begun. The same job that worked just fine before.

I had to start pinging upstream library and ecosystem people, on GitHub and privately, to start making sense of what was happening. Eventually, we collectively concluded that GitHub must've shortened the lifetime of their OIDC identity — it seems to have used to be 10 minutes long (at some point in the past) and is now 5 minutes, apparently. It's not documented clearly, and we have not been able to get any clarity by attempting to contact GitHub through private channels, using personal connections.

body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7.0.0 to 8.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to false.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

title: support variable-sized cells for healpix
body:
- [x] Tests added
- [x] User visible changes (including notable bug fixes) are documented in `changelog.md`

`healpix-geo>=0.0.9` (partially) supports the `"zuniq"` indexing scheme, which encodes the depth together with the cell ids. This allows variable-sized cells, but only for a subset of the features: conversion from / to geographic coordinates and deriving the cell vertices.

Anything else will require more thought, as most if not all other functions will need to return some sort of ragged array.

title: ignore the lock file
body:
The pixi lock file has not really been built to support dynamic versions, which causes pretty frequent updates of the lock file. To avoid that, this removes the lock file.

This means that every CI job has to resolve the dependency for all platforms, which causes a lot of overhead. To avoid that we'd need to copy the workflow from pydata/xarray#10888, but it may be even better to wait until that has been converted to a github action.
